transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

My whole sense of worth feels tied up in what I weigh and how my body looks, and it’s taking over my life. It has gotten to the point where I can't even focus on my job or enjoy being at home because this obsession is constantly running in the background.

To help me understand better, how has this affected your eating habits—for example, do you strictly limit your food intake, or do you experience episodes of eating large amounts of food in a short time?

I try to rigidly restrict my food during the day at work, but in the evenings, I end up eating a massive amount of food in a very short time. For example, I'll plow through half a pizza, cereal, and snacks in under an hour, even if I'm not really hungry. Once I start, it feels like something switches off in my brain and I am completely unable to stop.
After these episodes of eating a large amount of food, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

Yes, after those nights where I eat way past full, I end up making myself throw up or taking extra laxatives to 'fix' it so it doesn't show on the scale the next morning. It has become a weekly cycle for the last few months, sometimes happening even more than once a week if work is really stressful.
To help me understand your physical health, could you tell me your current height and weight, or if your weight is currently considered significantly below normal for your height?

I don't know my exact height and weight off the top of my head, and I try not to focus on the specific numbers. But my weight is generally in the normal range, and I'm definitely not significantly underweight.
How long has this pattern of binge eating followed by throwing up or using laxatives been occurring? Has it been happening at least once a week for three months or longer?

Yes, it's been going on for about seven months now, ever since I took on a much bigger renovation project at work. It definitely happens at least once a week, sometimes more during stressful weeks, so it has been a regular pattern for well over three months.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all the diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (ICD-10: F50.2). She experiences recurrent episodes of binge eating characterized by consuming large amounts of food in a short period with a subjective sense of loss of control. To prevent weight gain, she regularly engages in inappropriate compensatory behaviors, specifically self-induced vomiting and laxative misuse. These behaviors have occurred at least once a week for seven months (exceeding the 3-month threshold). Her self-evaluation is unduly influenced by body shape and weight, and her weight remains within the normal range, ruling out Anorexia Nervosa.
